subject: using whole linear predictor of one variable as a part of linear predictor of other variable

messages.author: 58acd2f2d6929a53
messages.subject: using whole linear predictor of one variable as a part of linear predictor of other variable
parts:
I have been utilizing the copy feature to use (multiples of) parts of linear predictor for one variable as a part of other variable (shared parts being either coefficients or spatial fields, as described in Virgilio's book).

Now, I am wondering if it is possible to use a (multiple of) complete linear predictor of one variable as a part of the linear predictor for other variable.

For instance, somthing like this:
X_i~Poi(m_i)
Y_i~Poi(M_i)

log(m_i)=eta_i=b_0+b_1*z_i+u_i
log(M_i)=a_0+a_1*w_i+a_2*eta_i

where u_i is a spatial random effect, z_i and w_i are fixed covariate values, b_0, b_1, a_0, a_1, a_2 are unknown coefficients.

All the Best
 Marek

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] using whole linear predictor of one variable as a part of linear predictor of other variable
parts:
you can. the construction is to use an iid model to equal the linear
predictor, then use the iid term further, and with copy to get it
scaled.

lin.pred=a + b*x

then define

0 = -epsilon + a + b * x

here, 0, are the Gaussian observations with high fixed precision, and
epsilon is iid model with fixed low precision.

then

log(m) = epsilon

log(M) = 1 + w + copy.of.epsilon


so you need 3 likelihood models in this case.

as far as I recall, there should be an examples in the book of Virgilio
or the SPDE book.

H
